newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa Plastics to issue T$4.2 bln bond.
newsitem.headline: Formosa Plastics to issue T$4.2 bln bond.

text.p: Taiwan's Formosa Plastics Corp will issue T$4.2 billion worth of five-to-seven-year unsecured corporate bonds in late October to raise funds for operations, lead underwriter Grand Cathay Securities said on Tuesday.

"Formosa bonds' weighted average coupon rate, at an all-in-cost 6.76 percent (semi-annual), will be the lowest by any Taiwanese firm so far this year," Albert Ting, senior vice-president at Grand Cathay, told Reuters.

Teco Electric and Machinery in mid-April issued T$1.5 billion of seven-year unsecured corporate bonds with a semi-annual coupon rate of 7.04 percent, while Walsin Lihwa Corp in mid-July issued T$1 billion of seven-year bonds with a semi-annual rate of 6.97 percent, Ting said.
"Now that the long-term rate for corporate bonds is below seven percent, many potential issuers have shown keen interest to launch their issues," he said.

Formosa's bonds will strip equally into three tranches, each accounting for T$1.4 billion -- with the five-year tranche at a rate of 6.80 percent per annum, the six-year one at a rate of 6.86 percent and the seven-year one at 6.94 percent, Ting said.
It will be the third time so far this year Formosa Plastics Group, Taiwan's largest industrial conglomerate, issued corporate bonds, he said.
Nan Ya Plastics Corp, another key Formosa Plastics group member, issued T$5 billion and T$4 billion of bonds in March and June, respectively, Ting said.
